stories.headline: Pakistan's Iran-US mediation effort peaks: Naqvi in Tehran, Trump credits Islamabad, US congressman praises Munir and Shehbaz
stories.summary: Pakistan's ongoing diplomatic mediation between Iran and the United States reached a high-visibility moment this week as Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi made a second successive Tehran visit (May 16-17) and met Iranian President Pezeshkian, following Field Marshal Asim Munir's earlier April trip. US President Trump publicly said the Iran ceasefire was done 'as a favour to Pakistan,' praising Munir and Shehbaz Sharif, while Congressman Jack Bergman sent a formal letter of appreciation. PM Shehbaz called Pakistan's role 'a shining moment in history' and spoke with Qatar's PM, who endorsed the effort. The week also saw contested reporting—CBS News and other outlets alleged Pakistan allowed Iranian military aircraft to park on its airfields (potentially shielding them from US strikes), which Islamabad denied—and a Drop Site News investigation linking Pakistan's diplomatic standing directly to Imran Khan's continued detention.

stories.headline: India-Pakistan rhetorical escalation: Indian Army Chief warns of 'geography or history,' ISPR responds sharply; Munir's Operation Sindoor claims contested by FARA filings
stories.summary: Indian Army Chief General Upendra Dwivedi warned Pakistan at a May 16 event that if it continues to harbour terrorists and operate against India, it must decide 'whether they want to be part of geography or history.' Pakistan's ISPR responded the following day, calling the remarks 'provocative,' 'warmongering,' and 'irresponsible,' while urging India to learn to 'co-exist.' Separately, Field Marshal Asim Munir's May 10 Operation Sindoor anniversary speech—in which he warned India against any future 'misadventure'—drew extensive Indian media coverage and a response from India's navy chief. US FARA lobbying disclosures from the week of May 6-9, 2025, emerged in Indian media to contradict Munir's claim that India had sought the ceasefire, showing instead that Pakistan mounted 60 interactions with US officials over that period.

stories.headline: Imran Khan: solitary confinement challenged in court, PTI alleges torture and vision loss in one eye
stories.summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf founder Imran Khan's sister Aleema Khan filed a petition at the Islamabad High Court challenging his alleged solitary confinement at Adiala Jail, while PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja publicly claimed Khan has been tortured and has lost vision in one eye. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi joined a sit-in near the jail alongside Khan's sisters. Separately, the IHC gave lawyers a final May 20 deadline to present arguments in the £190 million case.

stories.headline: Wave of militant attacks kills dozens across Pakistan as army faces domestic security crisis
stories.summary: A series of attacks between May 7-15 killed more than 50 security personnel across Pakistan's northwest and Balochistan, even as the military garnered international attention for its diplomatic role. A suicide attack on an army camp in Bajaur killed at least 15 soldiers; five more were killed in Balochistan's Barkhan district during an IBO; and a separate TTP-claimed vehicle-borne attack on a security compound in northwest Pakistan killed eight or nine soldiers. Pakistani lawmakers from Balochistan described the security situation as resembling a 'civil war,' while Indian and Pakistani analysts noted the gap between the army's global diplomatic profile and its inability to suppress domestic insurgencies.

stories.headline: Pakistan-Afghanistan border tensions risk ceasefire collapse as TTP claims attacks and Kabul airstrike allegations resurface
stories.summary: Relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan deteriorated further this week, with TTP claiming a deadly attack on a security compound in northwest Pakistan that killed eight or nine soldiers, and Al Jazeera reporting that both sides have continued to strike each other despite a March ceasefire. The BBC published a report about the March 16 Pakistani airstrike on a Kabul drug rehabilitation centre—which the UN says may have killed more than 250—with families calling for a war crimes investigation. Pakistan summoned a senior Afghan diplomat after a TTP attack.

stories.headline: Pakistan tests Fatah-4 ground-launched cruise missile with 750km range
stories.summary: Pakistan's Army Rocket Force Command on May 14 conducted a training launch of the indigenously developed Fatah-4 ground-launched cruise missile, described by ISPR as capable of engaging long-range targets with high precision using advanced avionics and navigational systems. The test was witnessed by senior military and scientific officials; President Zardari, PM Shehbaz, and Asim Munir commended the launch.

stories.headline: PM Shehbaz announces China visit (May 23-26) as Pakistan-China digital and economic cooperation expands
stories.summary: Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar announced PM Shehbaz Sharif will visit China from May 23 to 26 for official talks, coming weeks after President Zardari's April 25-May 1 China trip. This week, Shehbaz met a Chinese business delegation and announced that Chinese firm IBI Beijing United Technology will establish its digital economy headquarters in Pakistan. The government highlighted AI Policy 2025 and 5G auction as part of a broader digital transformation push.

stories.headline: PPP-PML-N coalition tensions: Bilawal rules out 28th Amendment talks, flags budget difficulties, viral press conference moment
stories.summary: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari this week denied that the government had contacted his party about any 28th Constitutional Amendment, and said the government could not pass either an amendment or the upcoming budget without PPP's support. He also constituted a PPP committee to negotiate the federal budget. Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar separately said he saw 'no indications' of the 28th Amendment. A viral video of Bilawal sharply cutting off PPP spokesperson Shazia Marri during a press conference dominated social media, with Marri later defending the exchange.

stories.headline: President Zardari holds dual investiture ceremonies conferring civil and military awards on dozens of recipients including Shahid Afridi
stories.summary: President Asif Ali Zardari presided over two investiture ceremonies at Aiwan-e-Sadr this week. On May 13, civil awards were conferred on recipients from journalism, sports, literature, and public service—including the Hilal-e-Imtiaz for former cricket captain Shahid Afridi. On May 14, 47 military awards were given to officers and soldiers for bravery and meritorious service, including posthumous awards for three martyred personnel.

stories.headline: PCB Chairman Naqvi's potential India visit for ICC meetings raises political questions amid post-Operation Sindoor tensions

The dual role of Naqvi as both interior minister and PCB chairman was highlighted as a complicating factor.
